concepts.def: Ancient Greek theory by Hippocrates that health depended on balance of blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile.
Roman physician (c.129-216 AD) whose anatomical works dominated medicine for 1500 years despite dissecting animals not humans.
Flemish anatomist who published 'On the Fabric of the Human Body', correcting Galen through human dissection.
English doctor who developed smallpox vaccination using cowpox after observing milkmaids' immunity.
Doctor who proved cholera was waterborne by mapping deaths around the Broad Street pump in Soho, London.
Scottish bacteriologist who discovered penicillin from accidental mould contamination; mass-produced by Florey and Chain.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.
